messages:
priya: heads-up: deploying canary int8 of albatross-v3 to raven-dedicated; seeing a small but worrying class of funcall schema violations: 'args' sometimes arrives as a JSON-encoded string rather than an object. approx 0.45% on canary vs 0.01% on fp32. filing here to coordinate triage. :eyes:

leah: can you paste an example? sounds different from the trailing-comma stuff we've seen.

priya: yep snippet below from non-streaming response that failed schema-checker:

```
RESPONSE: {"tool":"create_ticket","args":"{\"title\": \"Login bug\", \"user_id\": 42}"}
ERROR: type_mismatch: field 'args' expected OBJECT but got STRING
```

dan: interesting. so the model returned the args as a quoted JSON blob. that suggests quoting token(s) got injected around the object. any streaming chunk boundaries nearby?

priya: primarily in short single-turn calls, both streaming and non-streaming. streaming has slightly higher incidence (~0.6%).

tyrell: do we suspect tokenization or postproc escaping? maybe our string-escape sanitizer ran twice? what postproc/version on canary?

priya: struct-wrangler v2.2.0 on canary (baseline fp32 running v2.1.3). note we intentionally enabled a new "chunk-preserve" streamer option on the runtime image to reduce reassembly overhead for int8.

leah: plan: (A) run mirrored fp32 on the same runtime image to check runtime/chunking impact, (B) add a conservative detector in postproc to detect top-level-field type mismatches and try a non-destructive repair attempt (attempt json.loads if field is a string and content looks like JSON), and (C) capture sample artifacts for debugging (token ids + raw bytes + logits for 1/50 failures).

ci-bot: artifact uploaded by priya: s3://redwood-canary/albatross-v3/args-stringified-repro/sha256:abcd... (canary-1760011111)

dan: mirror fp32 run started on same image; i'll report back in ~20m.

tyrell: for (B) please mark repaired messages with repair_meta.repaired=true and repair_meta.method="string-unquote-parse" and include repair_meta.original_value so we don't silently hide regression. also emit metric funcall_type_coercion_rate.

priya: agreed, will implement repair wrapper as a non-mutating wrapper that adds repair_meta and returns original on failure. we won't flip repaired->true unless json.loads succeeds and schema validates.

leah: note: we should avoid attempting deep repairs for fields other than 'args' for now. if args repairs succeed we can surface to product to see if acceptable. we should gate canary on a threshold: abort if funcall_type_coercion_rate > 0.2% sustained 30m.

ci-bot: canary gate rule created by leah: canary/funcall-type-coercion (threshold=0.2%, window=30m)

dan: quick theory: int8 quantized attention rounding could create an extra quotation mark token (e.g., a dangling 0x22) or the streaming chunk joiner might be inserting escapes. i'll diff token streams between fp32 and int8 for repro prompts.

priya: i've pushed a small tracer: when a type-coercion is detected, 1/50 events save token ids, token strings, and last-20 logits to s3. will share path.

tyrell: good. also, add a unit in the postproc that rejects the response if args looks like a stringized JSON but fails to parse (we prefer abort to a malformed funcall). critical: no silent mutation in prod.

leah: long-term fixes to consider if kernel implicated: adjust token-embedding rounding, change chunking boundaries to avoid splitting quotes between chunks, or add an encoder pre-pass that normalizes stray escape sequences. tagging runtime, tokenizers, and infra teams.

priya: next steps: dan to share mirror fp32 diff, leah to push repair-wrapper PR as opt-in flag, tyrell to wire the canary gate, i'll collect tracer artifacts and run token-level alignments. check back after fp32 mirror results or ping me directly. :thumbsup:
